source.label: Uniform-disc fit to the February 2020 VLTI/MATISSE continuum data

controls.label: MATISSE reconstruction
controls.notes: An image of the photosphere reconstructed by the public SQUEEZE code from public VLT/MATISSE visibilities and closure phases of 8 and 19 February 2020, in the 3.94-4.00 micrometre continuum, convolved to the 4 milliarcsecond interferometric beam and cast onto a sphere of the published radius, so nothing finer than the beam is shown. Its bright and dark patches are not confirmed as surface features: a spotless disc reconstructed from the same coverage, at sizes within 2 percent of the star's, leaves patches up to as strong. Negating every closure phase fits equally well, so which limb is brighter is weakly constrained. The colours are a legend for reconstructed relative intensity in one infrared band, the paper's heat scale: not colour, temperature or albedo. The faint halo outside the disc is the same reconstruction's light beyond the photosphere, a fifth of the flux: half of it within one beam of the limb, the rest extended emission the visibilities require. The far hemisphere and the poles were not observed.

legend.title: Relative intensity at 4 µm
legend.meta: fraction of the brightest point · 1st–99.5th percentile stretch

controls.label: Polarised dust · December 2024
controls.notes: The photosphere as the MATISSE reconstruction shows it, with the dust around it: the degree of linear polarisation VLT/SPHERE-ZIMPOL measured in the V band on 3 December 2024, released by ESO as Phase 3 collection BETELGEUSE-B beside Montargès et al. (2026). The patches one to about 4.5 stellar radii out are starlight scattered by dust. This is their own Fig. B.1 given depth: the same inferno colour map on the same zero-to-0.10 scale, carried as four emission channels so a line of sight emits the bar colour of its own measured degree. The colours are a legend for a ratio, not the colour of the dust. The instrumental polarisation measured beyond eight radii is subtracted, so the empty sky is darker here than in the printed figure. The map is a sky-plane image with no third axis, so it is placed in the plane of the sky through the star and spread along the line of sight by the scattering-angle efficiency of polarised light; that depth is a convention, not a measurement.

legend.title: Degree of linear polarisation
legend.meta: V band, 3 December 2024 · the paper's own inferno scale

controls.label: Great Dimming clump · December 2019
controls.notes: The same photosphere, with the dust clump Montargès et al. (2021) fitted to the Great Dimming, drawn from the numbers they published for December 2019: a sphere of uniform density south and slightly west of the star and between it and us. Its extinction is scaled so the line of sight through its centre dims the star ten times, as they report for the southern hemisphere, and the light it scatters back is drawn faintly over that. A model fitted to images, not an image.
